stem:
Meera visits a science museum in Jaipur and sees four old time-measuring devices. Her teacher asks her which statement correctly matches a device to the observable change it uses to show the passage of time.
Which statement is correct?

options.text: A sundial shows time by the changing position of the shadow cast by sunlight.
A sundial keeps showing time at night by the shadow it casts without sunlight.
A candle clock measures time because its flame grows dimmer as time passes.
An hourglass measures time by water flowing from its upper bulb to its lower bulb.

teacher.key_rationale: A sundial indicates time through the changing position of a Sun-cast shadow; without sunlight (B) no shadow forms, a candle clock relies on marked burning of wax rather than flame brightness (C), and an hourglass uses sand, not water (D). Key recalculated as A, mirroring the source key position.
